A Snapshot of Your Day
You will be part of an open-minded team of 19 engineers where cooperation, supporting and developing each other, is a matter of course. As we have a lot of interfaces, you will have many contacts both internally and externally. There are great opportunities to delve into pipe design and / or calculation or to choose to become good at a more general level and perhaps in the future take on a role as a coordinating resource for other pipe design / calculation resources in our development projects.
How You’ll Make an Impact
Design pipe systems and produce manufacturing data in NX, as well as associated technical documentation
Participate in development and maintenance work / projects regarding product standards, technical solutions and functions and contribute to the technical solutions being / becoming cost-effective and quality assured
Collaborate with procurement and sub suppliers to develop good technical solutions, solve generic issues including root cause analyzes, finalize/update technical documentation
Responsible for installation questions in our order projects by working in the 3D tool NX
Together with the entire project team, make sure to carry out the design work according to the current schedule.
Create, review and update investigations / documentation within your technical area.
You will have a large network of contacts throughout the organization
Collaborate with the customer order department and sales department within your technical area.

What You Bring
MSc or BSc in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent knowledge or experience.
Good knowledge in common norms and standards applicable for process and mechanical engineering and design, specifically PED and ASME.
Experience in pipe design as well as performing and evaluating piping stress calculations is meritorious.
Good English language skills are required. Swedish language skills are meritorious.
You thrive in a changing environment with many challenges and like to work in a multicultural environment
You have a strong interest in technology and learn new things.
You have a very good ability to work in a team, you are structured, driven, take initiative and can prioritize and organize your work in an effective way.
You try to find solutions and feel an ownership of your tasks

About the Team
The team you will be part of consists of 19 people from all around the world and different backgrounds. We strive to support each other and build a strong technical knowledge within the team. There is always someone to discuss solutions and ideas with within the team before presenting the final scope. An internal mentorship program is set up to take care of new team members.
Our Gas Services division offers Low-emission power generation through service and decarbonization. Zero or low emission power generation and all gas turbines under one roof, steam turbines and generators. Decarbonization opportunities through service offerings, modernization, and digitalization of the fleet.
We can offer you employment benefits such as: reduction of working hours, advance vacation, health care allowance and an eventual possibility to a flexible working place.
Who is Siemens Energy?
At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100,000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation. 
Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation. 
Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo
Our Commitment to Diversity
Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity, we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences.
Application
Don’t hesitate – apply via https://jobs.siemens-energy.com/en_US/jobs , id nr 305673 not later than 2026-11-12
Ongoing selection is applied, the role might be filled before last application date.
We refrain from all contact with staffing and recruitment companies, or advertising brokers.

Transport is at the core of modern society. Imagine using your expertise to shape sustainable transport and infrastructure solutions for the future. If you seek to make a difference on a global scale, working with next-gen technologies and the sharpest collaborative teams, then we could be a perfect match.
Product Quality Case builder, Digital domain and Wheel loaders
We are looking for a Product Quality Case builder for the domain of Digital services and products, as well as for parts of the Wheel loader systems and components. As a case builder you will monitor the field quality situation of the domain in question and work closely with the respective Product Maintenance teams and the sales regions to drive product quality of our products.
This role offers a chance to significantly impact the quality of our products and thus our business.
Main Responsibilities:
The primary responsibility of the Product Quality Case Builder is to, in a fact based way, define and quantify product quality issues. You will monitor field statistics and other input on all markets to identify issues, initiate Quality Cases and also drive the cases in Define and Measure phase. This includes creation and interpretation of in-depth statistical data and information, perform prioritization among related quality issues and request technical material via the parts return process.
The Case Builder supports the Product Maintenance team throughout the cases, participating in PM and TFR meetings. You will chair the cross functional Field quality meetings.
In addition, the role also includes to initiate and/or evaluate Special Commitments and analyze data for decision, calculate costs for Special Commitments and support the Service Bulletin work.
You should contribute with your competence and expertise, collaborating closely and cross functionally in your network. We strive to put people in the driver seat by building a culture that is both self- and collaboration-driven. Besides the operational responsibility, you are expected to question the status quo, look for continuous improvements in ways of working and inspire and motivate your peers.
Required competencies:
We prefer if you have a Bachelor of Science within Engineering or equivalent. Experience of the Volvo Digital Services and products and Wheel loader product line-up is required. Strong analytical skills good communication and networking capabilities complete the picture.
You are fluent in written and spoken English. Additional languages are a plus.
The location for this position is in Europe.
Ready for the next move?

jobs.description:
Dignus Medical specializes in recruiting doctors, specialists and nurses for the healthcare sector across Scandinavia. We help solve staffing challenges by matching the right professionals with the right employers – at the right time. This year, we proudly celebrate our 20th anniversary. Watch our anniversary film (https://vimeo.com/1114843079?share=copy) and join us on our journey!
Have you been considering a career change but have not yet found the right opportunity?
Are you looking for a position where you can work across a broad range of surgery, take responsibility, and at the same time enjoy a healthy work-life balance? Then this could be the opportunity for you.
We are looking for a Specialist in General Surgery to join a smaller acute care hospital located on a Nordic island in a unique setting. Here, you will have the opportunity to work broadly within surgery and become an important part of a close-knit clinical team.
About the position
The surgical department offers a broad scope of practice and is not divided into narrow subspecialty sections. This means you will work with a varied patient population and have the opportunity to use a wide range of your surgical skills.
The work includes gastrointestinal surgery, gallbladder and hernia surgery, colorectal surgery, proctology, endoscopy and acute surgery. Both open and laparoscopic surgery are performed.
Endoscopy is a natural part of the surgical practice and includes both gastroscopy and colonoscopy.
Working at a smaller acute care hospital means that the working day can vary considerably. You should therefore enjoy a broad surgical role and feel confident assessing and managing a range of surgical conditions.
Close collaboration and a supportive team
As a surgeon, you will become an important part of a smaller team where colleagues work closely together and support one another. Collegial support and guidance are available when needed.
We are not looking for someone who is expected to know everything. What matters is that you have broad surgical competence, sound clinical judgement, and the confidence to recognise when you may need support or wish to further develop your skills in a particular area.
The smaller hospital setting also gives you the opportunity to contribute your experience and play an active role in the continued development of the department.
Work-life balance
The position is located in a unique Nordic island environment, surrounded by the sea, archipelago and nature. It offers an attractive alternative for those seeking a different lifestyle from what is often associated with working at a large regional or university hospital.
For those who value both a professionally rewarding career and time for family, leisure and recovery, the location offers an attractive combination.
Qualifications
We are looking for a specialist who:
Holds an EU-recognised specialist qualification in General Surgery
Has broad surgical competence and experience
Has experience in gastrointestinal and acute surgery
Has experience in endoscopy, particularly gastroscopy
Is comfortable working both independently and as part of a team
Has good collaboration skills and a patient-centred approach
Is flexible and appreciates the variety that comes with working at a smaller acute care hospital
Has good English language skills
Has a strong motivation to learn Swedish. Language training is provided.

Experience in additional areas of surgery is considered an advantage.
Who are you?
You are a Specialist in General Surgery who appreciates the breadth of the specialty and enjoys working in a smaller clinical environment where collaboration, flexibility and responsibility are a natural part of everyday work.
You are confident in your professional role, collaborative and open-minded. You value being part of a close-knit team where colleagues support one another and where your experience and expertise can make a meaningful contribution to both the department and its patients.
You are also motivated to continue developing professionally and are happy to share your own knowledge and experience with colleagues.
What Dignus Medical offers you:
• Ongoing support from a recruiter before, during, and after your employment
• Assistance with obtaining Swedish authorization and specialist approvals
• Help with relocation, accommodation, and support for your family if needed
• Access to a free language course with a private tutor via Teams/Skype:
Interested?
If you are interested in this opportunity or would like to learn more, you are very welcome to contact us.
We would be happy to tell you more about the position.
We look forward to hearing from you!
You can also register your CV (https://dignusmedical-en.recman.page/login) or sign up for our newsletter (https://www.dignusmedical.no/en/sign-up-for-newsletter/) to stay updated on future opportunities.

Are you looking for a endocrinology position where you can combine broad clinical work, professional responsibility and a high quality of life?
This is an opportunity to work as a specialist in endocrinology in a close-knit Nordic healthcare environment, while living in a peaceful island community surrounded by nature and the sea.
About the Island
This Nordic island is home to approximately 30,000 residents and offers a safe, peaceful and family-friendly environment. With its beautiful archipelago, clean air and easy access to outdoor activities such as hiking, sailing and cycling, the island provides excellent opportunities for an active lifestyle outside of work.
For professionals considering relocation with their families, the island offers schools, daycare services and a welcoming community within a compact geographical area.
About the Role
As a specialist in endocrinology, you will have a broad and varied clinical role, assessing, treating and following patients with a range of endocrine and metabolic conditions.
The position requires a physician with broad specialist competence who is comfortable working independently and taking responsibility for clinical assessments and treatment decisions.
Your responsibilities may include:
Assessment, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with endocrine and metabolic disorders
Management of conditions within areas such as diabetes, thyroid disorders, osteoporosis and calcium metabolism, pituitary and adrenal disorders
Evaluation and follow-up of patients with both common and more complex endocrine conditions
Providing specialist consultations and clinical guidance when needed
Working independently while being an active part of the wider medical team
Close collaboration with colleagues across the medical department and other relevant specialties
Contributing specialist expertise to the continued development of the service

A Broad and Independent Specialist Role
As the healthcare organization serves the island's population, we are looking for an endocrinologist with a broad clinical profile who feels confident managing a varied patient population.
You should be comfortable making independent clinical decisions while also valuing close collaboration with colleagues. The endocrinology service works within a smaller team, with close cooperation with the wider medical department and other healthcare professionals.
The position therefore suits a specialist who appreciates both professional autonomy and the opportunity to work closely with colleagues across different areas of internal medicine.
Requirements
We are looking for a specialist who:
Holds an EU-recognized qualification in endocrinology
Has broad clinical competence within endocrinology
Has experience in the assessment, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of endocrine and metabolic conditions
Is confident working independently and taking responsibility for clinical decisions
Has a broad and flexible approach to specialist work
Enjoys working in a smaller team with close multidisciplinary and cross-specialty collaboration
Has strong communication skills and a patient-centered approach
Communicates well in English and is motivated to learn Swedish

Broad specialist role: Work with a varied range of endocrine and metabolic conditions.
Professional autonomy: Take an independent role while having close collaboration with colleagues across the medical department.
Close-knit environment: Become part of a smaller team where your specialist expertise makes a tangible contribution.
Nordic island lifestyle: Enjoy a safe, family-friendly community surrounded by nature and the sea.

Relocating to another country is a major decision. We support you throughout the process, from first contact until you are established in your new position.
We offer:
Personal and ongoing support from your dedicated recruiter
Assistance with authorization and specialist recognition when required
Support throughout the relocation process

Take the Next Step in Your Career
If you are a specialist in endocrinology looking for a broad clinical role with professional responsibility, close collaboration and the opportunity to make a meaningful contribution within a smaller healthcare setting, this could be the right next step for you.

jobs.description:
Why Join K.D. Feddersen Recycling Solutions?
K.D. Feddersen Recycling Solutions is looking for a Business Director who wants to lead, develop and shape a business area experiencing strong market demand. The company is part of the Feddersen Group, with operations worldwide and a particularly strong presence across Europe and the Baltic region.
We are looking for an ambitious and business-driven leader ready to take ownership of a Nordic business area and play a key role in shaping its future. This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys combining leadership, sales and strategic responsibility while creating lasting business impact.
Your Future Workplace
This is a rare opportunity to lead a Nordic business area with full commercial responsibility, combining sales leadership, strategic influence and operational execution. Reporting directly to the Nordic Board, you will shape the area's direction, drive profitability and strengthen the company's market position across the Nordics.
As Business Director – Recycling, you will hold full budget and P&L responsibility for the business area. You will lead and support employees across the Nordic region while remaining actively involved in customer relationships, key account management and business development.
The business area focuses on project sales, agency representation, tender processes, service operations and recycling solutions for industrial customers. With significant autonomy, influence and responsibility, you will play a key role in the continued growth and success of the Nordic organization.
Your New Challenge
In this role, you will have broad responsibility spanning leadership, sales and business performance. You will work both strategically and operationally with considerable freedom and close interaction with customers, suppliers and internal stakeholders.
Key Responsibilities

Drive sales performance and profitability with full budget and P&L responsibility.

Develop and execute the business area's strategy and objectives.

Lead customer meetings, negotiations and commercial activities across the Nordics.

Strengthen strategic customer accounts and build strong partnerships with suppliers and industry stakeholders.

Lead, coach and expand the Nordic team.

Prepare and negotiate commercial agreements, quotations and pricing proposals.

Drive continuous improvements in processes, systems and ways of working.

Participate in management team activities and report directly to the Nordic Board.

What Makes This Role Unique?

Real authority to shape and influence a SEK 100 million Nordic business.

High level of autonomy with direct impact on strategic and commercial decisions.

Opportunity to build, develop and expand your own team.

International exposure through collaboration with suppliers and stakeholders across multiple markets.

A highly visible role with significant influence on future performance and market presence.

Entrepreneurial culture with short decision-making paths and strong team spirit.

About You
We are looking for a commercially driven, ambitious and down-to-earth leader who enjoys combining sales, leadership and business responsibility. You have a strong business mindset, the ability to identify opportunities and the determination to turn plans into results.
Through professionalism, structure and energy, you create engagement internally while delivering sustainable business performance. You are equally comfortable discussing long-term direction with the board as you are leading commercial activities in the market.
Qualifications

Experience in B2B sales, preferably within project sales, technical sales or industrial sales.

Experience leading teams, projects or commercial initiatives.

Proven experience with budget and P&L responsibility.

Strong negotiation skills and confidence in customer-facing situations.

Fluent in both Swedish and English.

Preferred Experience

Experience working with international suppliers.

Knowledge of the plastics, recycling or process industries.

Proficiency in one or more Nordic languages.

Personal Attributes
You are someone who:

Takes initiative, drives results and thrives in a dynamic environment.

Navigates complex sales processes and drives opportunities from initial dialogue to signed agreement.

Is humble, approachable and enjoys staying close to both customers and colleagues.

Has the patience and persistence required for project-based sales cycles.

Has a genuine interest in industrial solutions, plastics, recycling, sustainability and process technologies.

At K.D. Feddersen Recycling Solutions, you will work in a close-knit team with short decision-making paths while benefiting from the resources and stability of a larger international organization.
The company is foundation-owned, creating a long-term perspective with stable ownership and sustainable investments in both the business and its people.
We're Here to Support You

We look forward to learning more about your background, ambitions and how you can contribute to the continued success of K.D. Feddersen Recycling Solutions.

We are looking for an ambitious, commercially minded Finance Lead to join a fast-scaling AI company backed by NVIDIA, Microsoft, and AWS, and to grow with it.
About Antrino
Antrino Labs is building the platform that makes every square meter intelligent.
The physical world runs on processes nobody can actually see. Goods move, machines idle, space goes unused, and decisions about all of it are based on samples, guesses, and reports written after the fact. Antrino lets any organization deploy vision intelligence into a physical space and get back what is actually happening there, as structured, real-time information it can act on.
We have grown from 6 people to a team of 28 in less than a year, closed our Seed round, announced together with Dagens Industri, and are registered with Inspektionen för strategiska produkter (ISP). Everything we build follows Privacy by Design.
The role
This is not a traditional accounting position. Half the job is making the financial foundation work exceptionally well: payroll, bookkeeping, tax, payments, reporting, and administration, together with our founders and external advisers. The other half is commercial: working with the founders on pricing, business models, cost structures, and where the company puts its money.
One day you might be running payroll and closing the month. The next, you could be modeling the economics of deploying our platform across hundreds of customer sites, finding a European innovation grant, or helping the CEO evaluate a new commercial opportunity.
What you will work on
• Bookkeeping, reconciliations, and monthly and annual closing in Fortnox.
• Payroll, benefits, reimbursements, VAT, and tax, together with our auditors and banks.
• Invoicing, supplier payments, accounts payable and receivable, and corporate cards (Mynt).
• Filings with Bolagsverket and Skatteverket, board materials, minutes, and shareholder documentation.
• Budgets, forecasts, cash flow and runway models, and reporting for leadership, the board, and investors.
• Unit economics across cloud, AI inference, hardware, and deployment, and the margins they produce.
• Grants and non-dilutive funding from Swedish and European programmes.
• Replacing repetitive finance work with AI and modern software, so the function scales without its overhead growing at the same rate.
Who we are looking for
You are early in your career, with a strong financial foundation and an appetite for far more responsibility than you have today. You might be at a Big Four or mid-sized audit firm, an accounting agency, or in finance operations at a growing company.
• Around 2–4 years in accounting, auditing, or financial operations.
• Solid command of Swedish bookkeeping, payroll, and compliance, and hands-on experience with Fortnox or similar.
• Strong analytical skills and a real interest in modeling and commercial analysis.
• Excellent Swedish and English, written and spoken.
You take responsibility for the outcome, not just the task. You know payroll and tax have to be right every time while almost everything else moves fast, and you can hold both. You do not wait to be asked before fixing a process or chasing an opportunity.
It is a plus if you have worked with startups or venture-backed companies, understand SaaS metrics and unit economics, or have applied for funding through Vinnova, Almi, or EU programmes. You do not need all of this. We care more about judgment and how fast you learn than about years on your CV.
Life at Antrino
You will join a team of driven, ambitious people who thrive at a fast pace and enjoy working together. We go to AI events, host our own, and end plenty of weeks with an afterwork. Things change quickly here, and everyone's work is visible in what the company becomes.
What we offer
• Direct work with the CEO and board members on financial and commercial decisions.
• Exposure to fundraising, investor relations, and international expansion.
• Potential participation in our stock option programme after the probationary period.
• Freedom to improve systems, challenge processes, and bring AI into finance work.
• AI events, afterworks, team activities, and travel when the business requires it.
• Occupational pension, insurance, and friskvårdsbidrag.
Process
1. Introductory conversation about your background and ambitions.
2. Finance and accounting conversation about your hands-on experience.
3. Practical working session on a realistic scenario in operations, forecasting, or a commercial decision. We care how you think.
4. Conversation with the founders about options and terms.
We review applications continuously. References may be requested at the final stage.
Apply with your CV and a short note on why you want to move beyond traditional accounting into helping build a technology company.

Job Scope 
High level purpose of function. 

A Senior Vision Automation Engineer in a cell manufacturing company plays a key role in developing, optimizing, reverse-engineering, and maintaining machine vision and optical inspection systems to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operations. They are responsible for programming, troubleshooting, and improving cameras, lighting configurations, and image processing algorithms, supporting both legacy production line re-commissioning and new vision system installations. The role also includes ensuring accurate data transfer, system connectivity, and smooth communication with PLCs, SCADA, and upper-level MES platforms to enable inline defect traceability, dimensional inspection, and digital integration. Close collaboration with production, engineering, and maintenance teams is required to identify and implement solutions that improve quality, throughput, and equipment uptime. A strong focus is placed on continuous improvement, safety, and scalability to meet the growing demand for electric vehicle battery production. 

Key Responsibilities 
Overall areas of responsibilities and activities 

Participate in HAZOP sessions and ensure compliance with process safety, operational safety, and environmental standards relating to equipment control and programming.  

Responsible for the FATs of the equipment (Project timeline dependent).  

Lead vision system integration and optical calibration during equipment commissioning and line re-starts (Project timeline dependent). 

Develop and reverse-engineer the vision inspection systems to be implemented in the production and logistics equipment in the factory, as well as the relevant specifications and documentation. 

Author and review engineering design documentation (Specifications, Functional design, Logic diagrams, Test Cases, Test Records).  

Train and mentor new engineers, and educate other support functions on machine vision, optics, and quality inspection gates. 

Code review and test of suppliers' vision software and algorithmic work within the projects to validate specified defect detection thresholds (Gauge R&R) and to ensure the quality and reliability of the data transferred from the equipment to the upper-level systems. 

Participate in R&D activities for piloting of new technologies and their suitability to production environments. 

Define and improve the factory blueprint, general specifications and ways of working in collaboration with the extended automation and digitalization teams. (Project timeline dependent). 

Contribute to technical improvements, development and optimization of software processes internally in the automation team 

The role requires regular presence on the production floor, with a minimum of approximately 25% of working hours spent on-site. Depending on project needs (such as line re-commissioning), there may be periods where up to 100% of working hours are required on the shop floor. 
Develop and maintain machine vision and image processing programming standards. 

Guide and mentor colleagues to industrial best practices, focussing on growth and development. 

Complete supplementary tasks as seen fit by management to effectively utilize time and resource for the benefit of the business. 

Requirements 
Educational background and previous experience required for the role 

Qualifications and Experience 

Masters Degree in Electronics, Mechatronics, Electrical, Automation, Robotics, Software Engineering or similar.

Assess business value, risk, and impact before and after changes

As part of building our Maintenance Engineering organization, we are expanding our team with a Process Equipment Engineer focused on our Furnace Area. This is an opportunity to contribute to a technically advanced manufacturing environment and play an important part in strengthening our capabilities within the Furnace Area.
Read more about Silex here.
The team and the area
You will be part of the Maintenance Engineering organization and report to the Maintenance Manager. The Teams purpose is to provide technical leadership for assigned equipment and work closely with Team Managers, Service Technicians, Maintenance Engineers, Process Engineers, Area Managers, and external suppliers.
The Furnace Area is an important part of our production and includes advanced high-temperature processes such as epitaxy, Low-Pressure Chemical Vapor Deposition (LPCVD), and thermal oxidation. These processes are used to grow and deposit controlled material layers and to form high-quality oxide films, making stable temperature profiles, gas flows, pressure, and equipment conditions essential to product quality and process repeatability. You will bridge equipment maintenance and process engineering, using equipment data, process results, and production feedback to identify causes of instability, improve uptime and utilization, and ensure that technical actions are coordinated across teams.
About the role
As a Process Equipment Engineer, you will be responsible for the technical health, reliability, and continuous improvement of equipment within the Furnace Area. Equipment is your primary discipline, supported by process knowledge that enables effective fault analysis, improvement work, and close collaboration with Process Engineers.
You will act as the technical lead for the assigned equipment, guide service technicians, coordinate technical escalations, and lead root cause analyses of downtime events and recurring failures. You will also develop equipment monitoring and preventive maintenance, define relevant KPIs, contribute to equipment purchases and upgrades, and serve as a technical contact for suppliers.
In this role, you will:

Act as the technical lead for assigned furnace equipment, guiding service technicians and leading complex troubleshooting, root cause analyses, and follow-up of corrective actions.

Manage technical escalation plans and coordinate equipment status, priorities, and actions with Team Managers, Process Engineers, and suppliers.

Use equipment and process data to identify causes of instability, define and follow up KPIs such as uptime, MTBF, and MTTR, and improve equipment monitoring through equipment dashboard and SPC.

Develop preventive maintenance routines, maintain technical documentation, and contribute to equipment purchases, installations, upgrades, and spare-part planning.

Lead equipment-related risk analyses and ensure LOTO and other safety requirements are reflected in maintenance routines, documentation, and training.

We are looking for someone who has:

A Master’s degree in a relevant field, such as Materials Science, Chemistry, Physics, Mechanical Engineering, Electronics, or a related discipline.

At least five years of relevant experience in manufacturing with strong equipment-related knowledge and an understanding of production processes. Experience in semiconductor or MEMS process development or manufacturing is an advantage.

Experience with root cause analysis, data analysis, SPC, quality-control methods, equipment monitoring, and preventive maintenance systems.

Proficiency in English, particularly in technical terminology and documentation. Swedish is considered as highly meritorious.

To thrive in this role, you enjoy working analytically and finding practical solutions to complex technical challenges. You take a structured and proactive approach to your work, communicate clearly with different stakeholders, and are comfortable guiding others. With several activities often running in parallel, you are also able to prioritize effectively and ensure that actions are documented and followed through.
What we offer you

The opportunity to work with cutting-edge MEMS technology and some of the most advanced equipment in the industry.

A technically challenging environment where you solve complex problems and continuously develop your expertise.

A varied role in which new challenges, technologies, and improvement opportunities make every day different.

About Silex
Silex is the world’s largest and most advanced pure-play MEMS foundry, headquartered in Stockholm. MEMS is present in nearly all modern technology, from personal gadgets to automotive electronics, medical monitoring and testing equipment, and thermal management systems. With a team of expert engineers, operators, technicians, support staff, specialists, and more, Silex brings the ideas and concepts of the industry’s leading MEMS innovators to life.
The recruitment process
We have an ongoing recruitment process and therefore encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible. To apply, please attach your CV and answer a few questions. Our process is competency-based and includes a personality and logic test as well as reference checks. Additionally, we will conduct a background check and drug test prior to employment, and as an employer, we perform random alcohol and drug tests for all employees.

How do you secure renewable energy assets where industrial control systems, cloud platforms and cybersecurity come together? At OX2, protecting wind, solar and energy storage facilities mean understanding both the technology behind energy production and the risks that come with connected systems. We are now looking for a OT Security Lead to take ownership of our cybersecurity priorities with operational technology at the center and help shape how security is managed across our growing energy portfolio.
YOU WILL
OX2 is a renewable energy company developing, constructing, owning and operating large-scale wind, solar and energy storage projects. As the company expands its role as an independent power producer, cybersecurity is an important part of ensuring that its energy assets and the systems supporting them remain secure and reliable.  As OT Security Lead, you will take overall responsibility for cybersecurity across OX2's IT and operational technology environments, with a clear focus on OT. You will work across industrial control systems, cloud platforms and corporate IT, setting security requirements and ensuring that risks are understood and addressed throughout the development and operation of energy assets.
You will make risk-based decisions about which security measures are needed, where they should be implemented and how they should be prioritized across different facilities. Working closely with plant engineers, IT teams, suppliers and senior stakeholders, you will translate security requirements into practical solutions that work in operational environments.
Your main responsibilities will be to:

Own and prioritize the CSMS pipeline across OX2's wind, solar and energy storage assets.

Define security architecture and requirements across OT and IT, including SCADA, plant control systems, remote sites, Azure, AWS and SaaS environments.

Apply IEC 62443 and security principles such as zones and conduits, secure remote access, least privilege and security by design.

Establish and enforce cybersecurity requirements for suppliers, technology partners and external service providers.

Assess cybersecurity risks in vendor selection, acquisitions and divestments, contributing to cyber due diligence.

Govern external security partners and managed security service providers, including incident response and security delivery.

Translate NIS2 and relevant cybersecurity legislation into practical security measures across the business

The role involves collaboration across OX2's international business.

YOU ARE 
You have a strong background in cybersecurity. You understand the challenges of protecting systems where security, availability and operational requirements need to work together. Experience with MSSP governance, incident response or cyber due diligence is particularly valuable.
You are naturally curious and enjoy exploring new technologies and approaches to security. You make well-founded decisions. Experience from energy, utilities, industrial automation or other critical infrastructure environments is particularly valuable, but not essential if you bring strong practical OT security experience.
At OX2, you will have the opportunity to influence how cybersecurity is managed across an international portfolio of renewable energy assets. You will work close to the technology behind energy production, with the responsibility and autonomy to develop security capabilities that protect both current operations and future assets.
WANT TO KNOW MORE?

ABOUT OX2
OX2 is a renewable energy company accelerating the transition to a sustainable energy system. Through its integrated model as an independent power producer (IPP), OX2 develops, constructs, owns and manages renewable energy assets across onshore and offshore wind, solar and energy storage.  With a diversified portfolio of approximately 33 GW across development, construction, asset management and operations, OX2 combines entrepreneurial project development with long-term ownership and value creation. Stable benefits, and the best benefit of all: the people. 30 days of vacation, occupational pension, healthcare allowance, parking, the option to work from home up to two days a week, regular after works and, most importantly, an engaged and inclusive team.

About us
Svea Solar Utility (“SSU”) is a leading Swedish solar IPP with currently 8 solar parks in operation, totaling 75 MWp, 2 parks under construction, totaling 125 MWp, and a development pipeline of over 3 GW across more than 100 projects.

Job Description
WHAT YOU’LL DO
As a Sales Advisor at H&M, you’ll play a key role in creating an outstanding customer experience. You’ll welcome customers, guide them through your store, and support them in finding what they need while showcasing our products. Acting in line with our values, you’ll contribute to both your own success and the success of the company.
You will:
Share your fashion and product knowledge to help customers make informed choices.
Collaborate with your team to deliver exceptional service at every step of the customer journey.
Ensure the sales floor and back of house are well-stocked, organized, and inviting.
Support with opening and closing of the store.
Represent yourself and the brand positively during all customer interactions.

Our stores are the heart of our company, where customers experience our brand firsthand. As part of the dynamic Store Team, every role—from Sales Advisors, Department Managers, Store Managers and Visual Merchandisers to Assistant Store Managers, Cash Office Responsible, and Delivery Responsible in larger stores—contributes to creating an inspiring and welcoming environment. We are looking for people with…
Experience in customer service within fashion, retail, or similar fields.

And people who are…
Passionate about fashion and delivering an exceptional in-store experience while promoting our products and driving sales.
Thriving in collaborative and dynamic environments.
Communicative, creative, curious to work with store technology, with a strong eagerness to learn and develop.
Flexible and action oriented.

H&M Group is a global company of strong fashion brands and ventures. Our goal is to prove that there is no compromise between exceptional design, affordable prices, and sustainable solutions. We want to liberate fashion for the many, and our customers are at the heart of every decision we make.
We are made up of thousands of passionate and talented colleagues united by our shared culture and values. Together, we want to use our power, our scale, and our knowledge to push the fashion industry towards a more inclusive and sustainable future.

WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE 
At H&M Group, we are proud to be a vibrant and welcoming company. We offer our employees attractive benefits with extensive development opportunities around the globe.
 All our employees receive a staff discount card, usable on all our H&M Group brands in stores and online. 
In addition to our staff discount, all our employees are included in our H&M Incentive Program – HIP. You can read more about our H&M Incentive Program here.

About Taigatech
We solve some of the most important problems in industry with AI and computer vision. With our connection to the latest research and academia, we take world-leading research in AI and computer vision and turn it into impactful solutions that help the wood industry increase yield, availability, and productivity.
Technology is reshaping our world. We believe the forest and wood products have an important role to play in a sustainable future, and AI is how the industry gets there.
We are a growing team in a comfortable office in central Gothenburg, working closely with many of the leading names in wood processing. Our systems run in production at sawmills and pulp mills in Sweden and abroad. There's no better time to join our journey than now.
Why this role exists
Our systems create value the moment their output reaches the customer's control system — a correction, a signal, something the line can act on.
What determines the results are a handful of decisions made early and made well: which signal, where it lands, what the line does with it, and how it behaves when something unexpected happens. Get those right and the implementation is small and quick.
Today that judgement is distributed between our own team and the automation partners we work with on each installation. We want someone to decide what the interface should look like, judge whether it came out right, decide when a sensor or other component needs replacing, and if the signal belongs on a different fieldbus.
That's the person we're hiring. You don't replace our automation partners. You become the one who leads them.
What you'll do
The role is both technical and leadership, and the balance shifts from project to project.
Own the machine-side interface. You decide how our system talks to the customer's PLC. Signals, timing, handshakes, watchdog, fail-safe behaviour. You write the functional description the work is built from.
Lead our automation partners. Sometimes that means writing the code snippet yourself. Sometimes it means explaining what needs doing and reviewing that it came out right. You decide which.
Make the technical decisions on the customer's plant. Upgrading a component for better results, or moving to a different fieldbus, is yours to propose and drive. The implementation itself normally goes to a partner.
Be the customer's main contact through the project — scope, timeline, status, time and cost reporting. You take over from sales and carry the delivery home.
Clear the path. OT network access, change control, and the dialogue with the site's automation and IT departments, so the installation can be done quickly and safely.
Work closely with our ML and vision engineers. Translate what the process needs into what the model has to output, and the model's limits back into what we can promise.
Make it repeatable. A reusable interface specification, a commissioning checklist, and a growing network of automation partners to deliver alongside.
Who you are
You need experience, but we don't care how many years you have behind you. We care about what you've done.
You have programmed PLCs in live production, on at least one major platform — Siemens TIA/S7, Beckhoff, ABB, Mitsubishi, Codesys or equivalent
You have hands-on experience of industrial networks: Profinet, Profibus, EtherCAT, Modbus TCP, OPC UA or equivalent.
You have extended control systems you did not write with retrofits onto existing, running equipment
You have written functional descriptions that someone else built from
You have stood on site during commissioning, with production running and someone waiting
Drives the project forward by keeping people accountable, asking the right questions, and pushing decisions when it matters — even when that means a difficult conversation.
Swedish and English, and you sometimes travel to sites
Bonus
Sawmill, pulp and paper, or other heavy process industry
Vision systems, sensors or measurement equipment
Experience on the supplier side, responsible for subcontractors
Machinery directive and risk assessment on modified lines
Python and basic data analysis
What we offer
You'll be our first dedicated automation hire. You set the delivery process, and it becomes the standard we scale on. As delivery volume grows, the function gets built around you.
You'll work directly with the founders, with our ML engineers and with the mills themselves. Office in Gothenburg.
We review applications on a rolling basis.
